controls.rule: Universe: every Highlands of Many Cultures (Finkelstein, Lederman & Bunimovitz 1997) catalogue entry on map 18-17, as listed in research/sources/full_reads_2026-10-12/highlands1997/page_coverage.csv PDF 838-884 (printed 803-849). Eligible: a ruin (khirbeh, tell-khirbeh, or unnamed building-remains site); excluded by type before ranking: villages, cemeteries, burial caves, springs/reservoirs, single rujm, shrine, isolated terrace, and the two targets. Excluded: any ruin whose grid lies < 1000 m from either target grid. Rank by the smaller Euclidean OIG grid distance to either target; take the first four. Grid source: exact OIG point from research/rarity/kohlit/stage1a/stage1a_units.csv (WBADB rows citing Highlands pages) where present, else the 1-km cell centre implied by the site number (map-square digits). Ties (equal metres) broken by Highlands number ascending; no ties occur among ranks 1-5 (rank 4 = 2239 m, rank 5 = 2688 m). Selection uses no described feature.
controls.size_criterion: Plan requires 0.2-1 ha. The repo's Highlands extraction records area only for Kh. Yanun (0.4 ha); no area for any neighbour is in the repo, and the 92 MB Highlands PDF cannot be read here. Frozen deferred rule: area is taken from the first record opened in step 2 that states the site's area (Highlands catalogue metadata, else ASI 1 entry). A control with a stated area outside 0.2-1 ha is replaced by the next site on the frozen ranking (alternates below, in order); a control with no stated area is retained and flagged size_unverified. Replacement depends on area only, never on features.
controls.prior_exposure_note: Before this file, the integrator read repo summaries of Highlands entries for 18-17 (page_coverage.csv, observations.csv, stage1a_units.csv, followup C section B). These contain brief feature descriptions of several sites; selection is by distance only. No JSP 9, ASI 1, map sheet, Guerin or imagery opened before this file.

key.assignment_method: Python secrets.SystemRandom shuffle of [TARGET, Kurum, Risa, Jarayish, Tana el-Fauqa] onto U1-U5

U4.site: TARGET: Kh. Yanun (18-17/43/01, P-a) + Yanun village (18-17/32/01, P-b)

answers.scorer_note: Scored from packet text only (U1.md-U5.md). No other file, source or outside knowledge used. R1 states (p. 12) that isolated tombs, cisterns and caves were listed separately and not published, so R1 silence is treated as non-evidence; no unit qualifies as NEGATIVE.

Q1.evidence: No cave, pit, cistern or tomb is mentioned (R1, p. 827); R4 'Traces of ruins.' only (p. 391); R2, R3 no entry.

Q2.evidence: No tomb or grave recorded in any record.

Q3.evidence: R1 re-checked pottery Iron I(?), Iron I-II, Iron II; 'No Hellenistic or Roman entry.' (p. 827). No other dated record.

Q6.evidence: R1 team did not visit and repeats an earlier fort description; isolated features unpublished; R4 identification by name only within a ~7 x 9 km square.

U1.label: SILENT
U1.confidence_reason: No record describes the zone at a scale that would show pits or tombs.

Q1.evidence: 'Foundations, caves, cisterns, and rock-cut tombs.' (R4, vol. II p. 245)

Q2.evidence: R4 lists cisterns and rock-cut tombs together but gives 'No count, dimensions, distances between features, or dates.' (p. 245). R1 sheikh's tomb is a shrine, not an ancient grave.

Q3.evidence: R1 pottery figure includes Hellenistic and Roman profiles (pp. 836-839); R3 sherds include Roman (p. 167). Roman not subdivided; nothing dates the cisterns or tombs themselves.

Q4.evidence: Features are listed in the ruin's own R4 entry, so presumably at the site, but no position or distance is given.

Q6.evidence: R4 names the feature types at the ruin but gives no positions, counts or distances; R1 and R3 do not mention them.

U2.label: PARTIAL
U2.confidence_reason: Opening (cisterns) and rock-cut tombs both recorded at the ruin, adjacency unknown; in-zone placement inferred from the entry, not stated.

Q1.evidence: Only 'shepherd caves' (R1, pp. 832-834); 'No pit, cistern or tomb is mentioned'. R2, R3, R4 no entry.

Q3.evidence: 150 sherds, EB II-III, MB(?), Iron II; 'No Hellenistic or Roman pottery is reported.' (R1, pp. 832-834)

Q6.evidence: Only R1 summary, which excludes isolated tombs/cisterns/caves by design; no other record covers the unit.

U3.label: SILENT
U3.confidence_reason: Single catalogue summary that by its own statement omits the relevant feature class.

Q1.evidence: Installation 38-7: [paraphrase: a rock-cut rectangular pit, 2.50 x 1.80 m, about 2.00 m deep, open at the top, plaster-lined] (R2, pp. 93-94; abstract 35*). Also columbarium 37 (rock-cut, p. 89), winepress vats, bone pits inside tombs. R2 p. 80 also notes cisterns in an unpublished 1998 ridge survey (no positions).

Q2.distance: about 5 m (38-7 lies about 5 m SW of burial cave 38-2)
Q2.evidence: R2 pp. 93-94; columbarium 37 is about 35 m S of tomb cluster 39 (pp. 89, 94).

Q3.evidence: Tomb 38-2 first cut in Phase I (late 2nd/early 1st c. BCE to Herod, late Hellenistic) and in use in Phase II (1st c. CE, Early Roman) per kokh pottery (pp. 81, 84-85, 94). Pit 38-7 itself is undated (only washed-in Roman sherds). Site level: P-a has Persian/Hellenistic 1, Roman 4 sherds (R1 pp. 828-831); R2 calls the area the hinterland of 'the Hellenistic and Roman settlement of this unit' (p. 94).

Q4.distance: excavated area about 650 m from P-b and about 1,150 m from P-a (both beyond 500 m on rounded grids; footprint spans two spurs so larger than one point)
Q4.evidence: R2 location statement. In-zone features: only R1's 'burial caves in its vicinity' at P-b (no count, distance or date, pp. 821-823); no in-zone opening recorded. A cistern site ~550 m from P-a (Iron I/I-II only, p. 831) is also outside. 1998 ridge-survey cisterns/burial caves have no positions.

Q5.evidence: Tomb 39-2 oriented south-north 'with its forecourt opening at the north end' (pp. 81-85). This is a tomb in cluster 39, not pit 38-7, and lies in the out-of-zone excavated area.

Q6.evidence: R2 records the excavated area at fine scale (metric dimensions, inter-feature distances), but that area is outside the zone; the zone itself is covered only by R1 summaries (isolated features unpublished) and R4 brief entries.

U4.label: SILENT-IN-ZONE
U4.confidence_reason: A full pit + adjacent (5 m) Hellenistic/Early Roman tomb exists but ~650 m from P-b; footprint extent, grid rounding and unlocated 1998 survey features leave some chance part lies within 500 m.

Q1.evidence: 'No cave, pit, cistern or tomb is mentioned' (R1, pp. 820-821); R4 'Traces of ruins.' only (p. 394); R2, R3 same-name sites excluded.

Q3.evidence: Rhodian stamped amphora handle; Hellenistic ~10%, Hellenistic-Roman ~8%, Roman ~15% of 39 sherds (R1, pp. 820-821).

Q6.evidence: Completely demolished ruin known only from an R1 summary (isolated features unpublished) and R4 'Traces of ruins.'

U5.label: SILENT
U5.confidence_reason: Period evidence exists but no record describes the zone at feature scale.
